$comment: Plans as data, and only what can be delivered. Version 1 sold an API quota and a custom scan cadence that did not exist. Version 2 sold what one mechanism delivers: a private GitHub repository the engine writes into. Version 3 (16.10.0) is paid by bank transfer against an invoice; the Dogecoin launch year is withdrawn from sale (Dogecoin stays for voluntary contributions on support.html); a one-off Field Brief is added; the written brief is defined; and a missed delivery now has a stated remedy.

delivery.summary: Each subscriber gets a private GitHub repository. The engine writes the subscriber's slice into it after every scan and opens an issue when something changed. GitHub supplies access control, notifications, history, downloads, its API and webhooks; none of it is rebuilt here.

what_github_provides.alerts: issues opened in the repository, delivered by GitHub notifications
what_github_provides.api: the GitHub API over your own repository, under GitHub's limits
what_github_provides.webhooks: repository webhooks you configure; they fire on every update

payment.statement: Bank transfer against an invoice, in USD or EUR. The invoice carries the order id, the amount and the bank details.

premium.name: Radar Premium
premium.for: an engineer, founder or analyst following a shortlist
premium.billing: invoiced monthly in advance, cancellable at any time

premium_pro.name: Radar Premium PRO
premium_pro.for: a lab, fund or company watching part of the field
premium_pro.billing: invoiced monthly in advance, cancellable at any time

field_brief.name: Field Brief
field_brief.for: a fund, company or lab that needs the open field on one desk
field_brief.billing: one invoice, paid before the work starts

definitions.watchlist_repositories: repositories you name, scanned with every public scan, in the map or not
definitions.field_watches: a standing query over new projects, e.g. 'any new EEG project using LSL'
definitions.digest: an issue opened in your repository listing what changed; none when nothing did
definitions.written_brief: the Field Brief: 10 to 14 pages, PDF and Markdown with a CSV appendix, written and checked by an analyst

sections: Builders and the teams behind them
brief.review: Every project in the brief is checked by an analyst; automatic false positives are named and kept out.
brief.sources: The Radar's published data, the repositories themselves, and public company sources such as registries, company sites and Crunchbase, each cited with its date.

provisioning.statement: Set up by hand for each subscriber once the transfer arrives. There is no billing backend; the first digest arrives within seven days of the payment arriving.

cadence.statement: Your list is scanned with the public scan, every three hours. There is no separate faster schedule.

never: Payment never buys inclusion in the public map.
Payment never changes a score, a tier or a piece of evidence.
Nothing on the public map is withdrawn to create a paid version of it.

we_guarantee: Your watchlist is scanned with every public scan, every three hours.
What changed is written to your private repository after each scan.
An issue is opened when something changed, and not when nothing did.
The first digest arrives within seven days of the payment arriving, or the payment is refunded in full.
A Field Brief arrives within five business days of the payment arriving, or the payment is refunded in full.
If the engine misses a day of deliveries, your term is extended by that day, and the gap is noted in your repository.
we_do_not_guarantee: That the public map, or any field watch, finds every BCI project that exists.
That a third-party repository is correct, maintained or fit for any use.
GitHub's own availability, or that a repository stays public, named or online.
That every project a field watch surfaces is relevant to you.

terms.Who invoices: The AxonOS Project / Denis Yermakou, in USD or EUR, with the order id on every invoice.
terms.Cancelling: Monthly plans can be cancelled at any time; the month already paid runs to its end.
terms.After cancelling: We stop writing to your repository and you keep it, with its history. Your watchlist is deleted from the engine within thirty days.
terms.Confidentiality: Your watchlist, your field watches and your brief are never published and never feed the public map.
terms.Liability: Limited to the fees paid in the twelve months before a claim.
